title: Will the old style come back?
summary: Barnes believes the old men could easily revive it but the young will not, and he dislikes today's music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Do you think anybody's gonna ever come back to that old style and play it again ever?

What, with the music? Yeah. Well, I'm gonna tell you something about that, Al. That's very easy to do. You catch the old man, Peter Barga, myself, old man, put him there. One or two days, make a rehearsal, just about two hours, catch some of the old music and go back and get it.
Yeah, but do you think any of the youngsters will ever get it?

Oh no, no, no, no, no. Music is going every day. We got a new music. The music they got today is nothing. Now you hear today, you hear them all hollering, hollering, you don't hear no music, you don't hear drum, you don't hear no drum. You hear cymbals blowing, blowing the big blue notes. You understand? But you don't hear no music like a voice and singing, you get on there and sing them. Them people, they're going, they're cutting everything. Brass and them, they'll be going to record. Well, I'll just say, it's a big orchestra. With the guitar, the cytop, the drum, and the drum. What kind of drum they got? They don't have drum as a drum. You get your one of them popped up. We played a drum uptown one time, we went to picnic. I remember what it was. The fellow come in and asked to play. All right, so I got them and let them play. We bust out a number and Lord, what happened? We had to stop the tune. Stop it. Tell them, tell them that we can't play this music. We know we're talented, maybe we don't play that.
